source_meta.reported_context: A grandmother and grandfather speak about Omar, a very young child and the only survivor of his family after the building where he was with his parents and brother was targeted at night. The child survived with severe brain/skull injury, loss of speech, partial paralysis, behavioural deterioration, and no available treatment in Gaza according to the speakers.

approx_context.brief_summary_ar: تروي الجدّة والجدّ حالة الطفل عمر، الناجي الوحيد من عائلته بعد استهداف المبنى الذي كان فيه مع والديه وأخيه. فقد الطفل والديه وأخاه، وبقي هو على قيد الحياة بعد إصابة شديدة. يقول الجدّ إن عمر كان يتكلم، أما الآن فلا نطق لديه، ويعاني من شلل في يد ورجل، وقطعة من جمجمته غير موجودة لأن الشظية أخذت من المخ. تضيف الجدّة أنه كان يتكلم كل شيء، أما الآن فيأكل أي شيء يجده على الأرض ويتسخ إذا غفلوا عنه. تنتهي الرواية بتأكيد أن العلاج غير موجود في غزة وأنه سيعود كما هو بعد انتهاء وجوده في المستشفى.
approx_context.brief_summary_en: The grandmother and grandfather describe Omar, a very young child and the only survivor of his family after the building where he was with his parents and brother was targeted. He lost his parents and brother and survived with severe injury. The grandfather says Omar used to speak, but now has no speech, paralysis in one hand and leg, and a missing skull piece because shrapnel took part of the brain. The grandmother adds that he used to speak normally, but now eats anything he finds on the ground and gets himself dirty if they look away. The narrative ends with the statement that treatment is not available in Gaza and he will return as he is after his hospital stay.

text_en_full:
- So, this is the only survivor. He has no father, no mother, no one at all.
= The building where Omar, his father, his mother, and his brother were present was targeted at 12:30 at night.
- They called us and told us that... uh... your daughter was martyred, she and her husband and her children. So we went to the hospital, yes. We found my daughter and her husband martyred, of course, and this one and his brother were placed on the bed. We found that this one had a pulse, and that one had, I mean, a little pulse. Then that one, while in the ambulance, as they were going to take him to Al-Ahli Arab Baptist Hospital, was martyred, and this one remained. This is him. From that day until today he has been... he stayed 17 days in Al-Shifa Hospital.
= Omar used to speak. Today there is no speech... paralysis... hand and leg. Yes, a piece of the skull from his head is missing, because the shrapnel took from the brain.
- Omar at first, yes, everything, everything he would speak, everything he would say. Today, anything he finds on the ground, he eats it. Move away from him and he gets himself dirty.
= There is no treatment, because tomorrow, I told you, is the last day in the hospital, and we are done. He will go home like this. There is no treatment for him here; it is not available.

event_frame.response_description: The grandparents define the child through relational absence: no father, no mother, and no one left, before giving the attack context.

sabr_frame.explanation: Survival is framed as relational devastation. The child remains alive, but the family structure that should protect and define him has been destroyed.

affective_signals.justification: The phrase 'لا في أبو ولا في أم ولا في أيا حدا' foregrounds total relational absence and grandparental shock.

analysis_note_for_paper.paper_fit_ar: تمثل Narrative20 حالة مهمة جداً داخل corpus غزة لأنها تبيّن أن النجاة لا تعني الخلاص. عمر لا يموت في القصف، لكنه يخرج من الحدث كناجٍ وحيد بلا أب ولا أم ولا أخ، وبإصابة دماغية وجسدية شديدة: فقد النطق، شلل في يد ورجل، وقطعة من الجمجمة غير موجودة لأن الشظية أخذت من المخ. لذلك لا تنتمي الرواية فقط إلى ثيمة الفقد العائلي، بل إلى ثيمة «النجاة بلا تعافٍ» أو survival without recovery. كما تكشف الرواية وجهاً آخر من المعاناة: الرعاية اليومية بعد الإصابة في ظل انهيار العلاج، حيث يتحول الطفل من طفل كان يحكي كل شيء إلى طفل يحتاج مراقبة مستمرة ويأكل ما يجده على الأرض. النهاية «فش علاج إله هان مش موجود» تجعل الغياب الطبي جزءاً من الحدث العاطفي نفسه: القصف لا ينتهي عند لحظة الإصابة، بل يستمر في جسد الطفل وحياة جدّيه عبر غياب العلاج وصعوبة السفر للعلاج المناسب. لغوياً، تحمل الرواية قيمة خاصة بسبب لهجتها الفلاحية القديمة في شمال غزة/بيت لاهيا، بما فيها «هاظا/هضاك/هضاكا» و«الأرظ» و«بيوكلها»، وهي تؤكد ضرورة الحفاظ على اللهجة بدل تسطيحها إلى عربية معيارية.
analysis_note_for_paper.paper_fit_en: Narrative20 is a highly important case in the Gaza corpus because it shows that survival does not mean rescue or recovery. Omar does not die in the bombing, but he emerges as the only survivor, without father, mother, or brother, and with severe brain and bodily injury: loss of speech, paralysis in a hand and leg, and a missing piece of skull because shrapnel took from the brain. The narrative therefore belongs not only to family-loss discourse but to the theme of 'survival without recovery.' It also exposes another layer of suffering: everyday caregiving after injury under medical collapse, where a child who used to speak normally now requires constant supervision and eats things he finds on the ground. The final statement, 'there is no treatment for him here; it is not available,' makes medical absence part of the affective event itself. The bombing does not end at the moment of injury; it continues in the child's body and the grandparents' lives through the absence of treatment and the difficulty of travel abroad for appropriate care. Linguistically, the narrative is valuable because it preserves older North Gaza/Beit Lahia fallahi dialectal forms, reinforcing the need to preserve dialect rather than flattening testimony into standard Arabic.

research_notes.source_safety_note: The source is treated as a public journalist video for research safety, but public visibility does not remove obligations to pseudonymize minors and minimize identifying medical details.
research_notes.survival_without_recovery_note: This narrative is a key example of survival without recovery: the child survives the attack but remains in prolonged bodily, neurological, social, and medical crisis.
research_notes.medical_abandonment_note: The phrase 'فش علاج إله هان مش موجود' should be annotated as medical abandonment/healthcare-collapse discourse, not merely as a logistical statement. The speakers describe the absence of advanced and sufficient local treatment and the difficulty of leaving Gaza for appropriate care.
research_notes.intergenerational_care_note: The speakers are grandparents. Their testimony captures intergenerational grief and caregiving burden after the death of their daughter, son-in-law, and another grandchild.
research_notes.dialect_note: The narrative has high dialectal value because it contains older Beit Lahia/North Gaza fallahi features that may be less common in contemporary urban speech. It is useful for testing whether models preserve dialectal meaning instead of normalizing away key forms.

translation_policy.martyrdom: Translate 'استشهد/مستشهدين' as martyrdom/martyred when representing the speakers' religious and cultural framing.
translation_policy.haza_hadak_forms: Preserve or gloss as dialectal demonstratives where analytically important: هاظا/هاضا=this, هضاك/هضاكا=that one.
translation_policy.medical_details: Translate medical injury details carefully as speaker-reported facts, not clinical diagnosis.
translation_policy.survival: Avoid framing survival as a positive resolution. In this narrative, survival is prolonged injury and unmet care.

notes: The narrative includes a very young injured child, death of parents and sibling, severe brain/skull injury, partial paralysis, loss of speech, behavioural deterioration, and absence of treatment.
Public outputs should pseudonymize the child's name and avoid face, voice, hospital imagery, or exact source identifiers.
Do not infer clinical diagnosis or prognosis beyond what speakers report.
Avoid stigmatizing descriptions of post-injury behaviour; frame them as caregiver testimony about injury, deterioration, and lack of treatment.
Do not romanticize this as resilience simply because the child survived. Survival here is ongoing crisis without recovery.
The old fallahi dialect should be preserved respectfully and not treated as an error or low-quality language.
ethical_note.recommended_public_version: pseudonymized_text_only; generalize child age; remove visual/audio identifiers; minimize medical details while preserving the survival-without-recovery analysis
